### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**13** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/index.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class), SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **56** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f65c36fcca8c33d38c62104c0888c950a315089a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ee71a0f3d639314dfb908adf4d01d739c25a08b9` — the merge of head `ab5e59107ea32f637f691e576af7a7d139af4311` into base `f65c36fcca8c33d38c62104c0888c950a315089a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ee71a0f3d639314dfb908adf4d01d739c25a08b9 && git checkout ee71a0f3d639314dfb908adf4d01d739c25a08b9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f65c36fcca8c33d38c62104c0888c950a315089a ab5e59107ea32f637f691e576af7a7d139af4311 && git checkout -B drift-repro f65c36fcca8c33d38c62104c0888c950a315089a && git merge --no-ff ab5e59107ea32f637f691e576af7a7d139af4311

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f65c36fcca8c33d38c62104c0888c950a315089a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f65c36fcca8c33d38c62104c0888c950a315089a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 服务器启动时同步表结构（包括 `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1` 的迁移任务）现在也拿 `os migrate apply` 用的同一把数据库锁，同步完立刻放掉，不在运行期间持有。锁模块下移到 `@objectstack/objectql`，cli 从那里引用。
- **为什么改：** 多副本同时启动时各自读到同样缺失的表、各自建表。实测在 main 上三个迁移任务加两个普通启动会撞 `pg_type` 冲突，有表被建两次，而进程都以 0 退出。
- **风险与回滚：** 单节点没人争锁时只多一条语句，启动输出不变；SQLite/Turso 不拿锁。等锁最多等启动预算的一半（默认 60 秒），超时则这次启动失败并说明原因，不改任何东西。回滚即还原本 PR。
- **先看：** `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` 的 `acquireBootSchemaMigrationLock` 和 `start()` 里包住第 1 到第 3 阶段的 `try/finally`。
- **两分钟验证：** 读 `plugin-boot-schema-migration-lock.test.ts` 的六个用例，以及 cli 实库集成测试里新增的并发启动用例。
- **需要你做的：** 无，由席位落地。
- **席位意见：** ACCEPT。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:server#2 · Head-sha `ab5e59107ea32f637f691e576af7a7d139af4311` · 2026-11-09T03:14Z

1. **Shape:** draft to `main`, `Fixes #31715`; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; patch changeset for `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/cli`. 10 files, +624/−179. #31598's card item 2 is quoted under its own heading.
2. **Premise:** held. On main, barrier-aligned boots (three `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1` plus two ordinary) against one fresh Postgres gave a `pg_type` collision and a table created twice, and all exited 0. After: 0 duplicates in 5 runs.
3. **Read of the diff:**
   - **One lock.** Same function, name and PG key as #31714. The module moved to `@objectstack/objectql` (the lowest package both the boot and cli import), and `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migration-lock.ts` is now a re-export only. No second copy.
   - **Scope.** Taken in `ObjectQLPlugin.start()` just before Phase 1 and released in `finally` after Phase 3, so a refusal or throw between phases still releases it. It is never held while the server runs.
   - **Datasource.** Default datasource only. DDL on any other datasource is unchanged, and the PR body says so.
   - **No lock** under `skipSchemaSync`, or when the default driver has its DDL deferred (the new read-only `SqlDriver#schemaDdlDeferred`), because `os migrate plan`/`apply` takes the lock itself. This keeps a migrator from waiting on itself.
   - **Turso.** The face-answer table gains `schemaDdlDeferred: 'inherited'`. The lock never asks a non-pg/mysql face for Knex (round 2).
   - **Bound.** Half the plugin's start budget (60 s by default), so a queued boot refuses with the lock's own message instead of hitting the kernel's start timeout.
   - **`serve.ts`.** Untouched: `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1` is the same kernel boot.
4. **R3 exception (#31598 card item 2):** uncontended single node is one lock statement with no output, and single-boot output is identical to main. SQLite takes no lock.
5. **Gates:**
   - **Dev:** 79/79 derived gates exit 0, with 0 NOT-MEASURED and 0 UNRUN. Lint is clean, and typecheck passes for objectql, driver-sql, driver-turso and cli.
   - **Tests:** objectql 577 files / 11736 tests, driver-sql 246, turso 97, cli unit 406; live-PG pin 8/8.
   - **Ablations:** 4 unit pins and 2 live pins go red.
   - **Check-runs on this head:** 36 success, 17 skipped, 0 failed (one PR-body guard run was cancelled when the body edit re-triggered it; its rerun is green).
6. **Review rounds:**
   - **Round 1 (seat review).** The new method had been inserted between `installRegisteredSchemas`'s JSDoc and that method, orphaning the doc. It was moved above (comment placement only, 3fa9769b → 86ea712b).
   - **Round 2 (CI fail).** `Test Core (3/8)` went red on runtime `organization-ownership-boot-guard.turso-remote.kernel.test.ts` because `getKnex()` throws on the Turso remote face, so a remote Turso boot died before its sync. Root fix (86ea712b → ab5e5910): the lock reads the driver's own `SqlDriver#dialectName` first and asks for Knex only for `postgres` or `mysql`. A Postgres/MySQL driver whose `getKnex()` throws still fails loudly (no catch). New pins cover a throwing SQLite face (no call, `null`) and a throwing pg/mysql face (rejects), plus a boot pin. Measured: that runtime file red 2 → green 2/2; runtime turso files 9/9; cli `schema-migrate.remote-posture` 11/11.
7. **Open questions, ruled:**
   - (1) New public names: the objectql lock exports and `SqlDriver#schemaDdlDeferred` are accepted.
   - (2) Module home: objectql, not core.
   - (3) Wait bound: half the start budget is accepted.
   - Deviation: the forced one-row Turso face-answer entry (`Record<keyof SqlDriver>`) is accepted.
8. **Landing:** Clause-② is no and no governed path is touched, so there is no contract review face. Ordinary queue landing: `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`.
